catalog_quote: There is no phonemic tone in the language, nor are there other phonemic suprasegmental distinctions. Stress is realized in isolated words by a slight increase in loudness, vowel duration, and pitch. However, lexical stress does not carry a high functional load in the language. There are no known instances in which stress is contrastive. Generally, words tend to receive penultimate stress, although there are exceptions to this tendency. Thus we tentatively hypothesize that Tomoip exhibits non-phonemic penultimate stress. Whereas prefixes such as class prefixes, the causative prefix βa-, and the prefixes me- and te- carry stress when affixed to monosyllabic bases, proclitics such as number markers and subject markers do not. new_statements.rule_in_words: Non-contrastive word stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the phonological word; affixes (prefixes and suffixes, e.g. possessive and transitive suffixes) count toward the word so stress shifts rightward under suffixation (delkua-n [ˈdɛl.kuan] vs delkua-ʝo [dɛlˈkua.ʝo]); proclitics (number and subject markers) are outside the stress domain. Authors call the analysis tentative and note unspecified exceptions.
new_statements.exceptions: Authors state there are exceptions to the penultimate tendency but do not list them; proclitics do not count for stress; the possessive preposition e can bear stress as a separate word (Barlow 2024). No phonemic tone, no contrastive length.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word including affixes but excluding proclitics; realization described for isolated (citation-form) words. Corroborated by Barlow 2024 LLM 42 p. 42: 'Stress is generally penultimate, with affixes but not clitics counting for purposes of stress assignment.'
new_statements.identity_note: Both sources describe Tomoip (tqp, tomo1244) as spoken by a consultant born in Milim village, Pomio District, East New Britain; same variety as the Glottolog languoid, no dialect split noted.
